This bug is extremely strange. I'm not even sure it's a JAX bug yet. I've spent the best part of two days trying to track it down and I've had no success yet.

A few observations:
* lowering the XLA optimization level `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_backend_optimization_level=2` makes the problem go away. This makes me suspect that the MLIR change is actually innocent: it means that we feed slightly different input to XLA, which get compiled and optimized slightly differently.
* Initially, I was thinking "maybe this is a race condition". But I tried adding code to force the JAX computation to block until completion (by calling `.block_until_ready()` on all the variable outputs) and the bug still occurs.
* The bug *only* occurs if the pyom2 code runs *after* the JAX code. Not before!
* Apparently trivial changes that should not touch *any* array data also make the bug go away. e.g., I added, after the code blocking until the jax computation completes:

```
    for var in list(vs_state.variables.keys()):
        val = getattr(pyom_obj.main_module, var, None)
        if val is not None:
            h = np.ones_like(np.asarray(val))
```
and that makes the bug go away reliably! All this does is allocate *new* arrays that are disjoint from any that exist, and it does so after JAX is done running anything. So something odd is happening.

* I tried printing sha256sums of all of the pyom2 array state before and after the jax code runs.  There was no change. I can't even prove any inputs changed!

At this point I have very few tools left: I can't tell which part of the pyom2 state was corrupted or even if it *is* pyom2's state being corrupted.

The only tool I have left is to minimize the example even further, e.g., could we try to extract just the biharmonic friction kernel out of pyom2 so we can make an even smaller reproduction that is more self-contained? "Making the example smaller until I can understand it" is the only tool I have left. Any help you can give in minimizing the example further would be greatly appreciated.

Yikes, what a mess. Thanks for investigating.

> I tried printing sha256sums of all of the pyom2 array state before and after the jax code runs. There was no change. I can't even prove any inputs changed!

I tried something similar: I dumped the PyOM2 state to a pickle file and ran the routine on the pickled state in a different file that doesn't use JAX. You probably guessed it; no NaNs. So the PyOM2 state looks fine until the Fortran routine runs.

How about I compile some print statements into the Fortran code and see where things go haywire.

But you are right, this could also be a bug in f2py, gfortran, the Linux kernel, .......
I remember that JAX had some issues with wrapped Fortran code before, see #6471 and #6823. These are a bit different because it's a compile time hang on GPU, but they also involve Fortran code running through Python...

Anyway, I'll report back when I know where this manifests first.

Maybe [rr](https://rr-project.org/) can help? 
It records all instructions executed, and you can inspect the heap and stack at all times...

Yeah, I actually tried `rr`, but it doesn't work in VMs it seems (where I was debugging) so I put it aside. It's on my list of things to try on a real machine, but I've run out of time to look further at this for the moment.

Oh my god. I'm so sorry. This turned out to be a bug in PyOM2 :man_facepalming: 

The problem is this:

```fortran
 real*8 :: del2(is_pe-onx:ie_pe+onx,js_pe-onx:je_pe+onx,nz)
 ! some other stuff...

 do j=js+1,je
   do i=is+1,ie
    del2(i,j,:)= (flux_east(i,j,:) - flux_east(i-1,j,:))/(cost(j)*dxu(i)) &
                +(flux_north(i,j,:) - flux_north(i,j-1,:))/(cost(j)*dyt(j))
  enddo
 enddo
```

So `del2` is allocated, but then only written from `start+1`. Therefore the first element is *uninitialized memory*, which just so happened to consistently contain NaN values with this particular stack. *This is why it went away when you allocated other stuff before the routine*, you pushed it to a different location in memory that didn't have NaNs :grimacing: 

To make things worse, the value of `del2` at this location drops out later, so the bug is *only* triggered when the allocated memory contains NaNs (no finite value will trigger it).

Anyway, terribly sorry for wasting your time, and I promise to look closer before reporting next time.

I'm relieved you found it! We take wrong outputs very seriously.

In general, this is a bug that [MemorySanitizer](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/MemorySanitizer.html) would catch very easily. I don't know if MemorySanitizer works for Fortran code: we mostly use the LLVM/Clang version of msan on C++ code, but there's no LLVM fortran compiler yet so that won't work. Perhaps there is a GCC version that works for gfortran. I am eagerly awaiting an LLVM fortran compiler for this reason alone!

@soraros As I understand it, there's an old out-of-tree flang that is more complete but depends on a really old LLVM fork, and its in-tree successor (also `flang`) that can't yet generate code. The classic situation: choose either "deprecated" or "not ready yet". But it looks like progress is happening!

issue.body:
In the testing suite for [Veros](https://github.com/team-ocean/veros), we test for consistency with a Fortran reference code via `f2py`. For this, we essentially do this:

1. Do all variable setup in Python / JAX
2. Clone state to Fortran by doing `getattr(fortran_module, var_name)[...] = getattr(python_module, var_name)`
2. Run Python function that is being tested
3. Run corresponding Fortran function
4. Compare

Starting with JAX 0.2.27 I noticed that one test fails sometimes (~ every 3rd run) because the *Fortran* result has some NaNs sprinkled into it. I do not see this with older JAX versions or when using NumPy instead of JAX, so I have to believe that the JAX / XLA runtime is somehow meddling with the memory used by the Fortran routine. I have verified that what is being copied to Fortran (in step 2) is consistent between backends and does not trigger NaN outputs by itself. I have only tested this on CPU.

I'm at a loss how to debug this further. Maybe someone has a hunch what changed in 0.2.27 that could cause this?

@soraros As I understand it, there's an old out-of-tree flang that is more complete but depends on a really old LLVM fork, and its in-tree successor (also `flang`) that can't yet generate code. The classic situation: choose either "deprecated" or "not ready yet". But it looks like progress is happening!

issue.body:
Hey folks,

I tried updating our Brax version from `0.11.0` to `0.12.1` but noticed issues while doing that. Our trainer, which uses PPO and has been working fine until now, now freezes due to the `acting.Evaluator.run_evaluator` taking for ever to compile (literally, at least 12 hours). I've spent a couple of full working days chasing down this bug and there seems to be some pretty weird dynamics in play here, and thus I've not been able to narrow the issue down to a single underlying issue.

Here's the model I've been using:

<details>
<summary>Example script</summary>

```python
# ruff: noqa: ANN001, ANN202, FIX002, ERA001, PLR0913, PLR0914, PLR0915, PLR0917, TD003

from brax import envs
from brax.envs.base import PipelineEnv
from brax.envs.base import State
from brax.io import mjcf
from brax.training import acting
from brax.training import types
from etils import epath
import jax
from jax import numpy as jnp
import mujoco
from mujoco import mjx
import numpy as np
from robot_descriptions import fr3_mj_description
import time


def create_mj_model() -> mujoco.MjModel:
    franka_fr3_path = epath.Path(fr3_mj_description.MJCF_PATH)
    robot_spec = mujoco.MjSpec.from_file(franka_fr3_path.as_posix())

    for geom in robot_spec.geoms:
        geom.contype = 0
        geom.conaffinity = 0

    robot_spec.option.integrator = mujoco.mjtIntegrator.mjINT_IMPLICITFAST
    robot_spec.option.timestep = 1 / 1_000
    robot_spec.option.iterations = 6
    robot_spec.option.ls_iterations = 8
    robot_spec.option.disableflags |= mujoco.mjtDisableBit.mjDSBL_EULERDAMP

    model = robot_spec.compile()

    return model


class FrankaFR3(PipelineEnv):
    """Environment for training FR3 and DEX-EE to reach the target position."""

    def __init__(self, control_timestep: float = 1 / 50, **kwargs: dict) -> None:
        mj_model = create_mj_model()
        sys = mjcf.load_model(mj_model)

        kwargs["n_frames"] = 10
        kwargs["backend"] = "mjx"
        super().__init__(sys, **kwargs)

    def reset(self, rng: jax.Array) -> State:
        data = self.pipeline_init(self.sys.qpos0, jnp.zeros(self.sys.nv))
        obs, reward, done = jnp.zeros(7), jnp.zeros(()), jnp.zeros(())
        metrics, info = {}, {}
        return State(data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info)

    def step(self, state: State, action: jax.Array) -> State:
        data0 = state.pipeline_state
        data1 = self.pipeline_step(data0, action)
        return state.replace(pipeline_state=data1)


def main():
    environment = FrankaFR3()

    rng = jax.random.PRNGKey(0)
    key_env, eval_key, rng = jax.random.split(rng, 3)

    num_envs = 1024
    process_count = jax.process_count()
    process_id = jax.process_index()
    local_device_count = jax.local_device_count()
    local_devices_to_use = local_device_count
    device_count = local_devices_to_use * process_count

    key_envs = jax.random.split(key_env, num_envs // process_count)
    key_envs = jnp.reshape(key_envs, (local_devices_to_use, -1) + key_envs.shape[1:])

    episode_length = 600
    action_repeat = 1
    env = envs.training.wrap(
        environment,
        episode_length=episode_length,
        action_repeat=action_repeat,
        randomization_fn=None,
    )  # pytype: disable=wrong-keyword-args

    num_eval_envs = 128

    def make_policy(params: types.Params, deterministic: bool = False):
        del params

        def policy(
            observations: types.Observation,
            key_sample: types.PRNGKey,
        ) -> tuple[types.Action, types.Extra]:
            if deterministic:
                actions = jnp.zeros((*observations.shape[0:-1], env.action_size))
            else:
                actions = jax.random.uniform(
                    key_sample,
                    (*observations.shape[0:-1], env.action_size),
                    minval=-1.0,
                    maxval=+1.0,
                )
            return actions, {}

        return policy

    evaluator = acting.Evaluator(
        env,
        make_policy,
        num_eval_envs=num_eval_envs,
        episode_length=episode_length,
        action_repeat=action_repeat,
        key=eval_key,
    )

    metrics = evaluator.run_evaluation(None, training_metrics={})
    print(metrics)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
</details>

And here's what I've observed so far. First, when running this file, the compilation takes a long time. I have not run this particular script for more than 10 minutes, but the original training pipeline in our code base ran for >12 hours without the evaluation loop compilation finishing (it takes a couple of minutes with `brax==0.11.0`).
```shell
$ time python -m evaluator_compile_freeze
2024-12-27 15:31:01.399190: E external/xla/xla/service/slow_operation_alarm.cc:73]
********************************
[Compiling module jit_generate_eval_unroll] Very slow compile? If you want to file a bug, run with envvar XLA_FLAGS=--xla_dump_to=/tmp/foo and attach the results.
********************************
^C^\[2]    310662 quit (core dumped)  python -m evaluator_compile_freeze
python -m evaluator_compile_freeze  656.21s user 2.35s system 106% cpu 4:02.79 total
```

Second, I believe, although am not sure, that the underlying issue might have something to do with the mocap bodies in the environment. If I comment out the mocap code above, the code runs fine:
```diff
@@ -24,12 +24,6 @@ def create_mj_model() -> mujoco.MjModel:
         geom.contype = 0
         geom.conaffinity = 0
 
-    robot_spec.worldbody.add_body(
-        name="mocap-body",
-        pos=[0.5, 0.0, 0.5],
-        mocap=True,
-    )
-
     robot_spec.option.integrator = mujoco.mjtIntegrator.mjINT_IMPLICITFAST
     robot_spec.option.timestep = 1 / 1_000
     robot_spec.option.iterations = 6
@@ -61,8 +55,6 @@ def reset(self, rng: jax.Array) -> State:
     def step(self, state: State, action: jax.Array) -> State:
         data0 = state.pipeline_state
         data1 = self.pipeline_step(data0, action)
-        mocap_pos = data1.mocap_pos.at[0].set(data1.mocap_pos[0] + 0.01)
-        data1 = data1.replace(mocap_pos=mocap_pos)
         return state.replace(pipeline_state=data1)
```

```shell
$ time python -m evaluator_compile_freeze
{'eval/walltime': 34.80631756782532, 'eval/episode_reward': Array(0., dtype=float32), 'eval/episode_reward_std': Array(0., dtype=float32), 'eval/avg_episode_length': Array(600., dtype=float32), 'eval/epoch_eval_time': 34.80631756782532, 'eval/sps': 2206.495985975641}
python -m evaluator_compile_freeze  54.26s user 2.43s system 140% cpu 40.298 total
```
The reason I'm not sure about this connection is that the use of `mocap_pos` is not a culprit in itself: I tried to reproduce this issue by swapping the above environment with the [`Humanoid`-environment](https://colab.research.google.com/github/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/main/mjx/tutorial.ipynb#scrollTo=mtGMYNLE3QJN) from the MJX tutorial notebook, with similar mocap body added to it, and that compiled fine.

https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/6823 and https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/9651 seemed like they could be related and I tried running the code with `JAX_ENABLE_MLIR=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` (as suggested in the issues) but that did not fix the problem.

I also tried the recommended `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_dump_to=/tmp/foo`. I don't know exactly how to interpret the results for those, however. What I notice, though, is that the working run outputs files up to `module_0211.jit__...`, whereas the hanging run only outputs files until `module_0109.jit_generate_eval_unroll...`, which suggests that the compilation gets stuck at [`generate_eval_unroll`](https://github.com/google/brax/blob/69637a359463738140c1b850f61ad0088a23538b/brax/training/acting.py#L113-L119). I've manually verified that this is indeed the case.

Does anyone have pointers to how to fix or further investigate this issue?

My setup (I've installed `jax` with `jax[cuda12-local]` extras):
```
$ python -c 'import jax, brax, mujoco; print(f"{jax.__version__=}, {brax.__version__=}, {mujoco.__version__=}")'
jax.__version__='0.4.36', brax.__version__='0.12.1', mujoco.__version__='3.2.6'

$ lspci | grep NVIDIA
00:03.0 3D controller: NVIDIA Corporation AD104GL [L4] (rev a1)

$ lsb_release -a
No LSB modules are available.
Distributor ID: Ubuntu
Description:    Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS
Release:        24.04
Codename:       noble

$ uname -sm
Linux x86_64
```
